To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fascia dentate of the hippocampus reorganizes after entorhinohippocampal deafferentation and that this process includes the sprouting of commisural and crossed enthorinal fibres which form additional collaterals and boutons.
the lesion of one entorhinal area induces sprouting of single axons and that this process is layer-specific and is regulated by adhesion molecules, growth factors, and glial cells.

the fascia dentate of the rat hippocampus is a suitable model to analyze the molecular factors regulating lesion-induced plasticity and to study the role of axonal growth in the formation of plaques in Alzheimer disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of lesion-induced plasticity.
the analysis of the molecular mechanisms underlying neuronal plasticity and regeneration after central nervous system trauma.
the analysis of the molecular mechanisms of lesion-induced plasticity of the central nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sprouting processes observed after entorhinocortical lesion are not only a model of lesion-induced plasticity, but also a model for the sprouting processes involved in Alzheimer's disease.
sprouting of single axons is a general phenomenon following central nervous system trauma.
the sprouting of individual fibres in the fascia dentate after entorhial cortex lesion is a complex process involving several different molecular factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

sprouting of central neurons after a central nervous system lesion is a highly complex phenomenon involving multiple mechanisms and that it may play an important role in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease.
the sprouting of commisural and crossed enthorhinal fibres in the hippocampus is a highly organized process which may be regulated by several molecular factors.
sprouting of single commissural and entorhial fibers is a major mechanism of lesion-induced plasticity in the rat fascia dentata.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lesion-induced plasticity of the fascia denata involves the sprouting of unlesioned fibres and is regulated by molecular factors that may also be relevant for the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease.

lesion-induced plasticity in the adult mammalian brain is not only a process involving the formation of new synapses by sprouting of axon collaterals but also a process of axonal growth and formation of new axons.
the sprouting observed after entorhal cortex lesion is not a simple regrowth of severed axonal stumps but a complex process involving a reorganization of existing fibres.
